key_insight: Intermediate features from image-restoration diffusion models encode corruption-aware cues that, when paired with temporal modeling, enable accurate optical flow estimation on real-world degraded videos.
problem_solved: Optical flow models trained on clean data fail on real-world corruptions (blur, noise, compression). This work defines Degradation-Aware Optical Flow and closes the gap so dense correspondence can be estimated reliably from degraded video input.
method: Extract corruption-aware intermediate representations from an image-restoration diffusion model as auxiliary features for flow estimation.
Introduce temporal-awareness by fusing diffusion features across frames (e.g., temporal encoder / cross-attention) so the model learns motion cues absent in single-frame restoration features.
Train/fine-tune a flow estimator that leverages both standard image features and diffusion-derived corruption cues to produce robust dense correspondences on corrupted videos.
impact: Provides a practical route to robust optical flow in real-world video applications (e.g., autonomous driving, video editing, surveillance) by reusing diffusion restoration priors—reducing reliance on pristine training data and improving performance under common degradations.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input degraded frames → diffusion restoration backbone (highlight intermediate layers) → temporal fusion module → optical flow output (arrows).
Before/after examples: degraded frames with noisy/blurred input and corresponding improved flow overlays produced by DA-Flow.
Bar/line chart: flow error (EPE) across corruption types comparing baseline flow vs. DA-Flow.
Icon strip: visual symbols for corruptions (motion blur, sensor noise, compression) with short captions showing robustness gains.
paper_title: DA-Flow: Degradation-Aware Optical Flow Estimation with Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Jaewon Min, Jaeeun Lee, Yeji Choi, Paul Hyunbin Cho, Jin Hyeon Kim
